incoming.name: British monarchy
incoming.excerpt: William I was succeeded by two of his sons: William II, and then Henry I.

incoming.name: London
incoming.excerpt: In 1097, William II began the building of Westminster Hall, close by the abbey of the same name.

incoming.name: New Forest
incoming.excerpt: William's successor, William Rufus was killed in a suspicious accident while hunting in the New Forest in 1100.

incoming.name: Palace of Westminster
incoming.excerpt: The oldest existing parts of the Palace (Westminster Hall and the Great Hall) date from the reign of William I's successor, King William II.

outgoing.name: Archbishop of Canterbury
outgoing.excerpt: Within a few years he lost William's advisor and confidante, the Italian-Norman Lanfranc, Archbishop of Canterbury, who died in 1089.

outgoing.name: France

outgoing.name: Jew
outgoing.excerpt: Eadmer relates two incidents in which William Rufus either convinced converted Jews to return to Judaism, or attempted to do so.

outgoing.name: New Forest
outgoing.section: The unusual death of William II
outgoing.excerpt: Perhaps the most memorable event in the life of William Rufus was his death, which occurred while William was hunting in the New Forest.
